title: Communications with the public and prospecting

reading.h: One rule of thumb for the whole topic
reading.body:
FINRA Rule 2210 sorts every communication into one of three categories, and one sentence unlocks the topic: **audience decides the category; the category decides approval; the product decides filing.**

Get those three questions in order and almost every 2210 item falls out. First figure out who received it (that names the category). Then apply the approval rule for that category. Then check whether the product mentioned triggers a filing with FINRA. Keep those separate — a common trap blends 'approval' and 'filing' as if they were the same step.

**Correspondence** — a written or electronic communication to **25 or fewer retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period.** It needs supervision/review under Rule 3110 but **no principal pre-approval**, and it is not filed.

**Retail communication** — a communication to **more than 25 retail investors within 30 calendar days** (ads, sales literature, websites, seminar handouts, form letters, TV/radio, and static social-media content). It requires **prior approval by an appropriately qualified registered principal** before use.

**Institutional communication** — distributed only to institutional investors (members, banks, insurers, RIAs, RICs, benefit plans with 100+ participants, entities with $50 million+ in assets) and not meant to be forwarded to retail. It needs written supervisory **procedures**, not pre-approval, and no filing.

'Retail investor' means any person who is not an institutional investor — whether or not a customer. The 25-in-30 line is the single most-tested number here. Records are kept **3 years**.

reading.h: Filing with FINRA's Advertising Regulation Department
reading.body:
Filing is a separate question from approval. The timing depends on the firm and the product.

**New member firms** (the first year of FINRA membership) file any broadly disseminated retail communication **10 business days BEFORE first use.**

**File 10 business days BEFORE use:** retail communications about **investment company rankings** the firm created (Rule 2212), **bond fund volatility ratings** (Rule 2213), and **security futures**.

**File within 10 business days AFTER first use:** retail communications about **registered investment companies** (mutual funds, ETFs, variable annuities, UITs), **public DPPs**, and **CMOs** (Rule 2216).

**Exempt from filing:** correspondence, institutional communications, generic tombstone ads, prospectuses filed with the SEC (except Rule 482 fund advertisements, which ARE retail communications), press releases to the media only, and reprints of independent third-party articles.

All communications must be fair and balanced, present risks alongside benefits, and contain no exaggerated, promissory, or misleading statements and no omission of material facts.

**No predictions or projections of performance** — with narrow exceptions such as hypothetical illustrations of a mathematical principle (like compounding), investment-analysis-tool output, and reasonable-basis price targets in research reports.

**Testimonials** must disclose that the testimonial may not be representative of other customers, is no guarantee of future performance, and — if the person was paid more than $100 — that it is a **paid** testimonial. A testimonial on a technical matter must come from someone qualified.

**Recommendations** in retail communications need a reasonable basis and must disclose the firm's conflicts: ownership of options/warrants, market-making in the security, and any underwriting of the issuer within the past 12 months.

**Options** communications must be approved by a **Registered Options Principal (ROP)**, and any retail options communication that goes beyond a general description must be preceded or accompanied by the current **Options Disclosure Document (ODD).**

**Municipal** advertising (MSRB G-21) is approved by a municipal securities principal. **CMOs** (Rule 2216) must use the full term 'collateralized mortgage obligation,' may not compare a CMO to a certificate of deposit, and must disclose prepayment sensitivity. **Investment company** ads (SEC Rule 482) must show standardized 1-, 5-, and 10-year returns and state that past performance is no guarantee.

**Social media:** static content (a profile, a website, a pinned post) is a **retail communication** needing principal pre-approval; **interactive real-time** content (live chat, replies) is treated like correspondence/a public appearance — supervised, not pre-approved. All business communications must be retained regardless of the device used.

Cold calls to residences are allowed only between **8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. in the local time of the person being CALLED** — not the caller. On each call the rep must give their name, the firm's name, a phone number or address for the firm, and that the purpose is to solicit.

The firm maintains its own **do-not-call list** and must check the **National Do-Not-Call Registry** using data no more than **31 days** old. Two exceptions to the national list: an **established business relationship** (a transaction within the last **18 months** or an inquiry within the last **3 months**) and prior express written consent. A firm-specific do-not-call request overrides the business-relationship exception.

quiz.stem: A representative sends the same letter recommending a mutual fund to 40 retail customers over a two-week period. Under Rule 2210, this letter is:
options: Correspondence, subject to review but not principal pre-approval
A retail communication, requiring prior approval by a qualified registered principal
An institutional communication, because it went only to existing customers
A public appearance, because it contains a recommendation
quiz.explanation: A written communication to more than 25 retail investors within 30 calendar days is a retail communication and needs prior principal approval; 25 or fewer would be correspondence. Being an existing customer does not make a person institutional.

quiz.stem: An email is sent to 20 retail customers within a 30-day period. Under Rule 2210 this communication is classified as:
options: A retail communication requiring principal pre-approval
Correspondence, subject to supervisory review
An institutional communication
An advertisement requiring a filing with FINRA
quiz.explanation: 25 or fewer retail investors within 30 calendar days makes it correspondence, which is supervised under Rule 3110 but needs neither principal pre-approval nor a filing. More than 25 would make it a retail communication.

quiz.stem: A member firm creates a retail communication that ranks a family of mutual funds it distributes. When must it be filed with FINRA?
options: It is exempt from filing
Within 10 business days after first use
At least 10 business days before first use
Within 30 days after first use
quiz.explanation: Retail communications containing investment company rankings created by the member (Rule 2212), bond fund volatility ratings, and security futures must be filed at least 10 business days before first use. Ordinary registered-investment-company retail communications are filed within 10 business days after use.

quiz.stem: A retail communication that goes beyond a general description of options strategies must be:
options: Approved by a general securities principal only
Preceded or accompanied by the current Options Disclosure Document and approved by a Registered Options Principal
Filed with the SEC before use
Sent only to institutional investors
quiz.explanation: Options communications must be approved by a Registered Options Principal (ROP), and a retail options communication that discusses more than the general nature of options must be preceded or accompanied by the current ODD.

quiz.stem: A firm posts a paid customer testimonial on its public website. Which disclosure is REQUIRED?
options: That the testimonial guarantees similar results for other clients
That the testimonial may not be representative, is no guarantee of future performance, and, because payment exceeded $100, is a paid testimonial
Only the customer's full name and account number
No disclosure, because website content is exempt
quiz.explanation: A testimonial must disclose that it may not be representative of other customers' experiences and is no guarantee of future performance, and if more than $100 in value was paid, that it is a paid testimonial. Website static content is a retail communication, not exempt.

quiz.stem: A registered representative may make a cold call to a prospect's residence only during which hours?
options: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in the caller's local time
8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. in the called party's local time
8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. in the caller's local time
Any time, if the firm maintains a do-not-call list
quiz.explanation: Rule 3230 permits solicitation calls only between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. in the local time of the person being called, not the caller. The firm must also honor its do-not-call list and check the national registry with data no older than 31 days.

quiz.stem: Which of the following is EXEMPT from filing with FINRA's Advertising Regulation Department?
options: A retail communication about a public direct participation program
An institutional communication distributed only to banks and insurers
A retail communication about a CMO
A new member firm's television advertisement
quiz.explanation: Institutional communications are exempt from filing (they need only supervisory procedures). Retail communications about DPPs and CMOs are filed within 10 business days after use, and a new member's broadly disseminated retail communication is filed 10 business days before use.
